title: Light: the first day
summary: God speaks light into being and separates it from the darkness, calling them day and night. Evening and morning make the first day.

title: The vault of the sky
summary: God makes an expanse to divide the waters above from the waters below and calls it heaven.

title: Land, seas and plants
summary: The waters gather and dry land appears. The earth brings forth plants and fruit trees, each according to its kind.

title: Sun, moon and stars
summary: Lights are set in the sky as signs for seasons, days and years. The Astronomical Book of 1 Enoch (chapters 72–82) ties its 364-day calendar to these lights.

title: Sea creatures and birds
summary: The waters teem with living creatures and birds fill the sky. God blesses them to be fruitful and multiply.

title: Animals and man
summary: Land animals are made, then man in God’s image, male and female. Genesis 2 adds that the man is formed from the dust and the woman from his side.

title: The seventh day
summary: God rests from the work of creation and blesses and sets apart the seventh day. This is the first Sabbath.

title: The Fall and exile from Eden
summary: The serpent deceives Eve, and she and Adam eat the forbidden fruit. They are driven out of the garden. Genesis gives no date, so this timeline places it just after creation week by convention.

title: Cain kills Abel
summary: Cain, angry that God favors Abel’s offering, murders his brother. Genesis gives no date. Ussher places it in year 129, shortly before Seth’s birth.

title: Seth is born
summary: Adam is 130 years old when Seth is born, in place of Abel. Seth’s line carries the genealogy down to Noah.

title: Cain builds the city of Enoch
summary: Cain names a city after his son Enoch — the same city Genesis 4:17 mentions in passing, with no date. The Book of Jubilees places it in the opening year of the fifth jubilee since creation.

title: The Watchers descend to Mount Hermon
summary: In the days of Jared, two hundred Watchers led by Semjaza descend on Mount Hermon and swear a mutual oath to take wives from among the daughters of men. 1 Enoch gives no year for this, only Jared’s long lifetime; Genesis 6:1–4 recounts the same union of the “sons of God” and the daughters of men.

title: The Watchers teach forbidden arts
summary: Azazel teaches men to forge swords, knives, shields and breastplates, and shows women bracelets, cosmetics and the coloring of stones. Semjaza teaches enchantments and root-cutting; Armaros teaches how to undo a spell, and others reveal astrology, the constellations, and omens read in the clouds, the earth, the sun and the moon.

title: The giants turn violent
summary: The Watchers’ sons grow into giants so large that they exhaust men’s food, then turn on men and animals alike, eating flesh and drinking blood. The earth itself cries out against the lawlessness spreading across it.

title: The earth’s cry reaches heaven
summary: Michael, Uriel, Raphael and Gabriel look down, see the bloodshed below, and carry the earth’s complaint before God, naming Azazel’s forbidden teaching and Semjaza’s leadership of the fallen Watchers as its cause.

title: God judges Azazel and the Watchers
summary: Raphael binds Azazel in the desert of Dudael to await the final judgment; Gabriel turns the giants against one another in mutual slaughter; Michael binds Semjaza and his companions for seventy generations. God promises the earth will be healed and blessed once the violence they caused is cleansed.

title: The Watchers plead with Enoch
summary: The bound Watchers ask Enoch, now renowned for his righteousness, to carry their petition for mercy to God. He writes it down, but a dream vision shows him their true fate, and he must tell them instead that they will have no peace or forgiveness.

title: Enoch’s journeys to the ends of the earth
summary: Guided by angels, Enoch tours the farthest places of creation: the storehouses of the stars and winds, the mountain of God’s throne, the four hollows of Sheol that hold the dead, the tree of life, and the valley prepared for the final judgment.

title: Enoch’s vision of the Son of Man
summary: In a second vision, Enoch sees one called the Son of Man, also named the Elect One, standing beside the Head of Days. He will sit on God’s throne at the end of days to judge kings and the mighty and vindicate the righteous.

title: Uriel shows Enoch the courses of the heavens
summary: The angel Uriel reveals to Enoch the laws governing the sun, moon, stars and winds: twelve months of thirty or thirty-one days, four ninety-one-day seasons, and a 364-day year. Enoch writes it all down for Methuselah and later generations.

title: Enoch’s first dream: the earth is swallowed up
summary: Before he marries, Enoch dreams at his grandfather Mahalalel’s house that the sky collapses and the earth is swallowed into a great abyss. Mahalalel reads it as judgment for the world’s sin and urges Enoch to pray that a remnant survive.

title: Enoch’s second dream: the bulls, the sheep and the flood
summary: In a second dream, written down for Methuselah, Enoch sees history as a procession of cattle: a white bull and heifer for Adam and Eve, a black bull for Cain goring a red bull for Abel, and later a white bull, Noah, who builds a vessel that carries his family safely through the flood. The vision runs on past the flood to a future judgment and a new house gathering every surviving creature.

title: Adam dies
summary: Adam dies at the age of 930.

title: Cain is crushed by his own collapsing house
summary: In the same year Adam dies, Cain’s own house collapses on him and kills him — stoned to death by the very means he used on Abel, which Jubilees reads as the heavenly tablets’ rule of measure for measure. Jubilees gives no month or day, only “the same year” as Adam’s death; placed here the day after by convention.

title: Enoch’s final year with Methuselah
summary: Sent back to earth for one last year before his translation, Enoch tells Methuselah to preserve his books of wisdom for later generations, then gathers his children to reveal history’s full course in ten “weeks,” ending in a final judgment and a new heaven.

title: Enoch is taken
summary: Enoch, seventh from Adam, walks with God and is taken at 365 years so that he does not see death. Jude 14–15 quotes a prophecy attributed to him that also appears in 1 Enoch.

title: Noah is born
summary: Lamech names his son Noah and says he will bring relief from the toil of the cursed ground.

title: Noah’s wondrous birth alarms Lamech
summary: The infant Noah is born white-skinned, with eyes that light up the room, and rises to praise God as soon as he is born. Lamech, afraid the boy is not his own, sends Methuselah to find Enoch; Enoch explains that the Watchers’ sin has doomed the world to a flood, and that this child will bring comfort once it has passed. 1 Enoch gives no date for this scene; placed beside Genesis’s date for Noah’s birth, it falls 69 years after Enoch’s own translation (year 988) already shown earlier on this timeline, a gap neither text resolves.

title: The Flood begins
summary: In Noah’s 600th year, on the 17th day of the second month, the fountains of the deep burst open and the rain falls for forty days. This is the first dated day of the flood account.

title: The ark rests on Ararat
summary: Five months after the flood began, the ark comes to rest on the mountains of Ararat. Genesis counts the span as 150 days. On this 364-day calendar it is 152 days, because the third and sixth months have 31 days. Only 30-day months give exactly 150.

title: Mountaintops appear
summary: On the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains become visible.

title: The waters dry up
summary: On the first day of the first month of Noah’s 601st year the waters have dried from the earth, and Noah removes the covering of the ark.

title: Noah leaves the ark
summary: On the 27th day of the second month the earth is dry. Noah, his family and the animals leave the ark, and God sets the rainbow as the sign of his covenant. The whole flood lasted 374 days on this calendar.

title: Noah’s sons divide the earth by lot
summary: Noah gathers his sons and grandsons and, drawing lots from a writing kept in his own bosom, assigns Shem the middle lands around Eden, Sinai and Zion, Ham the lands south of the Gihon, and Japheth the lands north of the Tina river. Genesis 10 lists the same three territories without this ceremony. Jubilees dates it to its own 1569th year since creation, a count that by this point runs well ahead of the Genesis-based chronology this app uses elsewhere; rather than import that number directly, this timeline places the event a decade after the ark lands and well before Babel, without claiming to reproduce Jubilees’ own year count.

title: Babel and the scattering of nations
summary: Men build a city and a tower in Shinar. God confuses their language and scatters them. Genesis gives no date. Ussher ties it to the birth of Peleg, in whose days the earth was divided.

title: Abram burns the house of idols
summary: At sixty, Abram secretly burns his father Terah’s house of idols by night. His brother Haran rushes in to save them and is burned to death himself. Jubilees dates this directly from Abram’s own birth year (1936 AM in its own count); because Jubilees’ internal year count diverges from the Genesis-based chronology this app uses by Abraham’s generation, this timeline instead places the event using the 17-year gap Jubilees itself gives before Abram’s declared departure from Haran, counted back from the year this app already uses for God’s call of Abram.

title: Abram watches the stars at the new moon
summary: On the first night of the seventh month, Abram stays awake until morning watching the stars to read the year’s rains, then concludes that the sun, moon and stars are entirely in God’s hand and prays to be shown the right path rather than searching the sky for it — a quiet rejection of the astrology his own family practiced. God’s call to leave for the land he will be shown follows immediately after. Placed here, as with the previous entry, by the 2-year gap Jubilees gives before that departure.

title: God calls Abram
summary: At 75, Abram leaves Haran on God’s command, with the promise of land, descendants and blessing for all nations. This date assumes Abram was born when Terah was 130, following Acts 7:4, not when Terah was 70.

title: Sodom and Gomorrah are destroyed
summary: God destroys the cities of the plain with fire and sulfur, and Lot escapes to Zoar. In the same year Abraham, at 99, receives the covenant of circumcision.

title: Isaac is born
summary: Sarah bears Isaac when Abraham is 100, the son God had promised.

title: Mastema accuses Abraham, and Isaac is bound on the altar
summary: A voice in heaven testifies to Abraham’s faithfulness, and Mastema, described as “the prince of the watchers,” tells God that Abraham loves Isaac above all else and urges that Isaac be demanded as a burnt offering to test him. Genesis 22 tells the same binding of Isaac without naming who is behind the test; Jubilees supplies that detail. Not independently dated elsewhere on this timeline, it is placed here by the 50-year gap Jubilees gives after Abraham’s call.

title: Jacob and Esau are born
summary: Twins are born to Isaac and Rebekah when Isaac is 60. Jacob is born holding his brother’s heel.

title: Levi is ordained priest in a dream at Bethel
summary: Camped at Bethel, Levi dreams he is ordained priest of the Most High, with his sons after him, and wakes to find his father has clothed him in priestly garments. Jacob tithes everything he owns, and Levi is set apart to receive the tithe of the tithe, a law the text says is written on the heavenly tablets. Genesis 28 and 35 both describe Jacob’s visits to Bethel but say nothing of Levi’s priesthood beginning there. Jubilees gives the day of the month (the 14th) but not which month; placed in month 1 by this app’s usual convention for underdated events, in the same year this timeline places Benjamin’s birth below.

title: Benjamin is born; Rachel dies
summary: Rachel dies giving birth to her second son on the way to Ephrath. She names him Ben-oni, “son of my sorrow”; Jacob renames him Benjamin and sets up a pillar on her grave. Genesis 35:16–20 tells the same story without the date Jubilees supplies. This timeline places it using the 6-year gap Jubilees gives before Joseph is sold, counted back from the year this app already uses for that sale.

title: Jacob defeats the Amorite kings
summary: Seven Amorite kings ambush Jacob’s sons as they pasture sheep near Shechem. Jacob marches out with his servants, routs the kings, recovers the flocks, and imposes tribute; the kings serve him until the family goes down to Egypt. Nothing like this battle appears in Genesis. Jubilees dates it to one year before Joseph is sold, which is how this timeline places it.

title: Joseph is sold into Egypt
summary: At 17, Joseph is sold by his brothers to traders and taken to Egypt.

title: The Day of Atonement is instituted
summary: Jacob’s sons slaughter a kid and dip Joseph’s coat in its blood to convince their father that a wild animal killed him. Jubilees makes the tenth of the seventh month — the day that news reaches Jacob — the origin of the Day of Atonement: Israel is to afflict itself and offer a young goat on this date every year after, in memory of the grief Joseph’s brothers caused their father. Leviticus 16 and 23:26–32 give the Day of Atonement’s law without this origin story.

title: Joseph rises to power
summary: At 30, Joseph interprets Pharaoh’s dreams and is made governor of Egypt, ahead of seven years of plenty and seven of famine.

title: Jacob’s family moves to Egypt
summary: Jacob, aged 130, and his household of seventy settle in Goshen. Israel’s long stay in Egypt begins.

title: Moses is born
summary: A Hebrew baby is hidden in a basket among the reeds of the Nile and raised in Pharaoh’s household. Moses is 80 when he confronts Pharaoh, which puts his birth 80 years before the Exodus.

title: The first Passover
summary: On the 14th day of the first month at twilight, each household slaughters a lamb and marks its doorposts with the blood.

title: The Exodus
summary: Israel leaves Egypt on the 15th day of the first month. Ussher counts the 430 years of Exodus 12:40–41 from Abraham’s call, following Galatians 3:17, so this falls 430 years after year 2083.

title: Israel reaches Sinai
summary: In the third month Israel camps before the mountain and God calls them a kingdom of priests. Exodus 19:1 says they arrive on the same day, which many readers take to be the first day of the month.

title: The tabernacle is raised
summary: In the second year after the Exodus, on the first day of the first month, Moses sets up the tabernacle.

title: Moses’ farewell speeches
summary: On the first day of the eleventh month of the fortieth year, Moses begins to address Israel on the plains of Moab. The speeches make up the book of Deuteronomy.

title: Israel crosses the Jordan
summary: On the tenth day of the first month Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground under Joshua and camps at Gilgal.

title: Saul is anointed king
summary: Samuel anoints Saul as Israel’s first king. Ussher dates this to 1095 BC.

title: David becomes king
summary: After Saul’s death David is anointed king over Judah at Hebron, and later over all Israel. Ussher dates this to 1055 BC.

title: David takes Jerusalem
summary: David captures the Jebusite stronghold of Zion and makes Jerusalem his capital.

title: Solomon becomes king
summary: Solomon succeeds David and asks God for an understanding heart.

title: Work begins on the Temple
summary: In Solomon’s fourth year, on the second day of the second month, construction begins. First Kings counts this as the 480th year after the Exodus.

title: The Temple is dedicated
summary: The ark is placed in the Most Holy Place and God’s glory fills the house. Seven days of dedication came before the Feast of Booths on the 15th of the seventh month, which puts the start on the 8th (reckoned from 2 Chronicles 7:8–10).

title: The kingdom divides
summary: After Solomon’s death, Rehoboam’s harsh answer splits the kingdom into Israel in the north under Jeroboam and Judah in the south.

title: Samaria falls to Assyria
summary: Assyria captures Samaria and deports much of the northern kingdom. Ussher dates this to 721 BC.

title: Daniel and others are taken to Babylon
summary: Nebuchadnezzar’s first deportation carries Daniel and other nobles away from Jerusalem. Ussher counts the seventy years of exile from here.

title: Jerusalem and the Temple are destroyed
summary: Babylon burns the Temple, the palace and the houses of Jerusalem and breaks down the walls. Second Kings 25:8 gives the 7th day of the fifth month. Jeremiah 52:12 says the 10th.

title: Babylon falls
summary: Belshazzar’s feast is interrupted by writing on the wall, and that night Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians.

title: Cyrus decrees the return
summary: Cyrus of Persia lets the exiles go home and commands that the Temple be rebuilt in Jerusalem. Ussher dates this to 536 BC.

title: The second Temple is completed
summary: On the third day of the twelfth month, in the sixth year of Darius, the rebuilt Temple is finished and dedicated.

title: Ezra arrives in Jerusalem
summary: Ezra sets out from Babylon on the first day of the first month and reaches Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month of Artaxerxes’ seventh year, carrying the law.

title: Nehemiah finishes the wall
summary: The wall of Jerusalem is completed on the 25th day of Elul, the sixth month, in 52 days and despite opposition.

title: Jesus is born
summary: Jesus is born in Bethlehem in the days of Herod. Ussher’s date is 4 BC. The Gospels give no day or month, so month 1, day 1 here only means “this year”.

title: Jesus is baptized
summary: John baptizes Jesus in the Jordan and the Spirit descends on him. Luke dates John’s ministry to the fifteenth year of Tiberius, about AD 29.

title: The crucifixion
summary: Jesus is crucified outside Jerusalem under Pontius Pilate on the day of preparation for Passover, the 14th of the first month by John’s account. AD 30 and AD 33 are the years most often proposed. This timeline uses AD 33.

title: The resurrection
summary: On the third day, the first day of the week, the tomb is found empty and Jesus appears to his followers.

title: Pentecost
summary: Fifty days after the resurrection the Spirit comes on the disciples in Jerusalem. Counting 50 days from the 16th of the first month gives the 5th of the third month. The Book of Jubilees places the Feast of Weeks on the 15th of the third month, which would move this date ten days later.

title: John’s vision on Patmos
summary: In exile on Patmos, John receives the visions recorded in Revelation. Early Christian tradition (Irenaeus) places this near the end of Domitian’s reign, around AD 96. The text gives no date.
